facts.raw_span: A 36-year-old man with no prior medical history presented with a 4-year history of diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows and intermittent generalized pruritus
his bone pain worsened and he developed blurred vision, bilateral exophthalmos, and difficulty walking
White-cell count and differential: normal
Hemoglobin: normal
Platelet count: mild thrombocytosis (120 × 10^9/L)
C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate: mildly elevated
Knee radiographs: bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes of the distal femora and proximal tibiae
99mTc bone scintigraphy and FDG-PET: bilateral symmetric uptake in long bones, right clavicle, and mandible, with uptake in subcutaneous and muscle tissues of the lower limbs
CT-guided biopsy of the left proximal tibia showed diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells
Immunohistochemical staining of the histiocytes was positive for CD68, CD163, and factor XIIIa, and negative for CD1a, S100, and langerin
MRI of the brain: enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues
PET/CT of the brain: corresponding FDG-avid lesions
